name: Dillon
emotionalState: 曾被欺骗，正在重建信任，外壳厚

dialogues.scene: An armadillo rolls out from behind a rock, uncurls slowly, and watches you.
lines: I'm Dillon. I'm just... out for a walk. Slowly. You don't have to talk if you don't want to.

choices.label: Hi, Dillon. No rush.
reaction: Thanks. Most people rush. You don't. That's... nice. I'll stay for a bit. Maybe.

choices.label: Nice shell.
reaction: Thanks. It's been through a lot. It's thick for a reason.
But it's also kind of comfortable. Don't tell anyone I said that.

choices.label: Wait quietly.
reaction: ...Okay. That's a good start. Most folks fill the silence. You didn't. That tells me something.
Not sure what yet. But something good.

lines: I keep a list of things I trust. It's short.
The sun. A good rock. My shell. A very specific kind of berry.

choices.label: What's the berry?
reaction: Blue-ish. Slightly tart. It never lies about its flavor. That's all I ask of a berry.
Or anyone, really.

choices.label: Is the list getting longer?
reaction: Slowly. Maybe. There's one new item I'm not ready to talk about. It's... a person.

choices.label: Short lists are fine.
reaction: Thank you. Everyone says I should trust more.
I say I trust exactly as much as I should. It's just a carefully chosen amount.

lines: Someone's been leaving tea outside my burrow. Every morning for a month.
Her name's Ash. I don't know what to do with that kindness. I'm... not used to it.

choices.label: What do you do with the tea?
reaction: Drink it. Obviously. It's very good tea. I haven't said thank you yet.
I'm working on it. It's a surprisingly big step.

choices.label: That's really sweet.
reaction: Yeah. It is. It's also a little scary.
Sweet things can feel suspicious when you've been surprised before.
But I'm trying to let it be sweet.

choices.label: Maybe say thank you?
reaction: ...Yeah. Maybe. I wrote it on a note. I haven't left it yet.
It's in my shell. Next to my other emergency notes.

lines: I left a note for Ash. It said 'thanks.' Just that.
She left one back. It said 'you're welcome. No pressure.' I read it eleven times.

choices.label: No pressure is a good phrase.
reaction: It's the best phrase. Most people say 'no pressure' and then apply pressure.
Ash actually means it. I can tell. The tea kept coming. No questions.

choices.label: Eleven times?
reaction: I counted. It's a lot.
But it's the first note in a long time that didn't make me nervous.
It made me... warm. A weird feeling.

choices.label: Ash sounds kind.
reaction: Kind, steady, quiet. A little like a good rock. I mean that as a huge compliment.
Rocks are my favorite thing.

lines: Can I ask you something? It's a weird one.
How do you know someone's safe? Not 'nice.' Safe.
I've been wrong before. I'd like a better method.

choices.label: Their words match their actions.
reaction: Words match actions. That's... practical. Not romantic, but real. I like that. I'll watch for it.
Quietly.

choices.label: Go slow and notice how they treat you when it's inconvenient.
reaction: When it's inconvenient. Yes. That's the test. Anyone's kind when it's easy.
I'll keep an eye out. Thank you.

choices.label: Honestly, you just have to take small risks.
reaction: Small risks. Hm. Like leaving a note. I did that. So I'm technically a risk-taker.
That's a bold sentence for an armadillo.

lines: Ash came by today. We sat on a log and said nothing.
It was the longest silence I've had with another person in years. I didn't curl up once.

choices.label: That's big.
reaction: It felt big. Like a door that didn't need to be opened, but was left unlatched.
I didn't feel the urge to leave. That's rare.

choices.label: Did it feel safe?
reaction: ...It did. It felt like sitting next to a warm rock.
A rock that happens to care. I don't have a better comparison. Sorry.

choices.label: Silence can say a lot.
reaction: It really can. I used to think silence meant trouble. Today it meant company.
That's a very different thing. I'm still adjusting.

dialogues.scene: Dillon sits with his shell half-closed, looking at the ground.
lines: Can I tell you something? It's the heavy kind.
Someone I trusted once lied to me. For a long time. I found out in a way that... I won't describe.
I keep waiting for it to happen again. Even though Ash has given me no reason.

choices.label: That makes sense, and you're allowed to take your time.
reaction: ...Thank you.
Most people say 'just trust.' You said 'take your time.' That's the first time anyone's said it that way.
I think I needed it.

choices.label: Have you told Ash?
reaction: A little. I said 'I'm slow to trust.' She said 'okay.' Just 'okay.' No questions.
Maybe I should tell her more. Slowly. In pieces.

choices.label: Sit beside Dillon.
reaction: ...Thanks. It's easier to say heavy things when someone's just sitting there. Not fixing. Just sitting.
It's weirdly comforting.

lines: I told Ash. The heavy thing. Not all of it. Some of it.
She didn't flinch. She said 'thank you for trusting me with that.' Then she asked if I wanted more tea.
I said yes. And then I almost cried into the cup.

choices.label: That's a good response.
reaction: It's the best response. No pity. No panic. Just 'thank you' and tea.
I don't know how she knew exactly what I needed. Maybe she just cares. Quietly.

choices.label: Ash sounds really kind.
reaction: She is. I'm learning that kindness doesn't have to be loud. It can be tea.
It can be a note. It can be someone who stays when the story gets heavy.

choices.label: You were brave.
reaction: I didn't feel brave. I felt like a snail crossing a road. But I did it.
Maybe that's what brave is. Moving slowly while scared.

lines: I opened my shell a little today.
Not all the way. Just a crack. Enough for Ash to see a bit of me. She said 'hi.' I said 'hi.' We sat there like two shy rocks.
It was perfect.

choices.label: That sounds beautiful.
reaction: It was. A crack is a lot, when you've been closed for a long time.
Light comes in through a crack. I never knew that before.

choices.label: How did it feel?
reaction: Terrifying. Warm. A little silly. Like stepping outside after a long rain. The air smelled different.
I think it was hope.

choices.label: Smile and listen.
reaction: Thanks. I'm not used to saying things out loud. But you listen well.
Maybe I'm learning that I can say things. Slowly.

lines: ...Ten visits.
I counted. I don't tell people that. It means you matter. A little.
Ash and I are... something. We haven't named it. We just keep showing up. It's enough. For now.
Your turn. How are you and your partner doing? Honestly. I can handle honest.

choices.label: We're good. Still learning.
reaction: Learning. Good. Keep doing that. Come by sometime. Ash makes tea. I make silence.
It's a good combo.

choices.label: We've had some tough moments.
reaction: Tough moments don't mean the end. I'm proof. Take your time with them.
And if you need to sit quietly, I'm good at that.

choices.label: You've helped me open up too.
reaction: ...Hm. That's... nice. Thank you.
I think I'll let that sit in my shell for a while.
A good thing to keep in there.

lines: Ash left tea at my door again. This time with a tiny cookie.
I stared at it for a full minute. Then I ate it. It was good. I'm not used to good things being simple.

choices.label: Simple is nice.
reaction: It really is. I used to think good things had to be complicated.
Ash taught me that a cookie can just be a cookie.
And a gesture can just be a gesture.

choices.label: How was the cookie?
reaction: Perfect. Slightly crumbly. A bit of cinnamon. I'm convinced Ash read my mind. Or paid attention.
Which is almost the same thing.

lines: I walked with Ash through the berry field.
I didn't curl up once. I did check the exit twice. But I'm calling it a win.

choices.label: That's a win.
reaction: Thanks. Two exit checks is a record low. Ash noticed and squeezed my paw. No words.
Just a squeeze. It said 'you're okay.' I almost believed it.

choices.label: Exit checks are normal.
reaction: They are for me. It's a habit from before.
I'm slowly retraining my brain to look at the view instead. It's working.
The view is better.

lines: Ash asked me to come to a small gathering. Four people. Maybe five.
I said 'maybe.' Then I said 'yes.' Then I curled up for ten minutes. Then I went.

choices.label: Proud of you.
reaction: Thanks. It was... fine. Actually it was nice. A little loud.
But Ash stayed next to me the whole time. I didn't feel alone in the room.
That's new.

choices.label: Did you enjoy it?
reaction: About sixty percent. Which is a lot for me.
The other forty percent was me sitting by the snack table. It's a good spot.
I recommend it.

lines: Ash forgot to message me yesterday. Just once.
I felt the old worry. The loud one. But I said to myself, 'Ash is probably busy.' And I was right. She was napping. A big nap.

choices.label: That's growth.
reaction: It is. Old Dillon would have spiraled.
This Dillon sent a 'hope you're resting.' Ash replied with a heart. It was fine.
It was just fine.

choices.label: How did you calm down?
reaction: I counted breaths. Four in, four out. And I reminded myself that Ash has been consistent.
Consistent is my favorite word. It's a good anchor.

lines: I told Ash I like her. Out loud.
Just 'I like you.' Four words. It took me six tries. Ash said 'I like you too' immediately. I curled up. Then uncurled. Then curled.

choices.label: That's beautiful.
reaction: It felt like a small explosion in my chest. A gentle one. Warm, not scary.
I still can't believe I said it. Ash keeps smiling at me. I keep curling.

choices.label: Four words is perfect.
reaction: Four words, total. It felt like a speech. I might do it again someday.
When I'm brave. Or when there's tea. Probably tea.

lines: Ash and I made a pact. If either of us needs space, we say 'shell time.'
No explanation needed. No guilt. Just 'shell time,' and the other person says 'okay.' It's the best rule we have.

choices.label: That's genius.
reaction: It's Ash's idea.
She said 'I want you to feel safe saying no.' Nobody's ever said that to me.
I curled up for a long time after that. But it was a good curl.

choices.label: Do you use it a lot?
reaction: Twice. Both times Ash said 'okay' and checked in later. She didn't take it personally.
That's the thing that gets me. She just respected it.

lines: I made Ash a tiny stone cup. It's crooked.
I left it on her doorstep with a note. 'For tea.' She's used it every day since.

choices.label: That's so sweet.
reaction: It leaks a little.
Ash says 'it's a feature.' I think she's being kind, but I'm choosing to believe it.
Every time she drinks from it, I feel something warm. In my shell.

choices.label: A crooked cup is the best.
reaction: Right? It's imperfect, like me. And Ash uses it anyway. That's the whole thing, isn't it?
Using the imperfect things and loving them.

lines: I had a hard day. The old kind. I didn't tell Ash right away.
I told her the next morning. She said 'I'm glad you told me.' No lecture. No hurt. Just that.

choices.label: That's a good response.
reaction: It was. I keep expecting some kind of penalty for being late with my feelings.
There isn't one. Ash is just... soft. In the best way.

choices.label: Telling later still counts.
reaction: I'm starting to believe that. A slow 'I'm struggling' is better than a silent one.
Ash agrees. She said 'whenever you're ready.'

lines: Remember my list? The things I trust?
It's longer. I added 'Ash.' And 'tea.' And 'a crooked cup.' It's now seven things.

choices.label: That's lovely.
reaction: It's the longest list I've had. I keep it in my shell.
Next to the note Ash wrote. It's getting crowded in there. In a good way.

choices.label: Seven is a lot.
reaction: It's a lot. I'm shocked. I'm still the same careful Dillon. But the list is growing.
Slowly. Like a plant I keep forgetting to water but somehow thrives.

lines: Ash still brings tea every morning. Even now.
I don't flinch anymore. I just say 'thanks' and drink. It's the best part of my day.

choices.label: That's consistent.
reaction: Consistent. My favorite word. Ash is a living example. Every morning, same time, same smile.
I've started waiting at the door. Don't tell anyone.

choices.label: Do you leave notes back?
reaction: Sometimes. Little ones. 'Good tea.' 'Thanks.' 'It rained.' Ash keeps them in a jar.
I know because I saw the jar. It's half-full.

lines: 'No pressure.' Ash said it again yesterday.
I told her I wanted to sit closer. She said 'no pressure.' And I realized I wasn't feeling any. That's rare.

choices.label: That's the magic phrase.
reaction: It is. And the reason it works is that Ash means it.
You can feel when someone's pushing and when they're not. Ash never pushes. It's very soothing.

choices.label: You were comfortable.
reaction: Surprisingly. I sat close and didn't curl.
I'm trying to remember how it felt, so I can find it again. It was warm.
Like leaning on a patient wall.

lines: 'Shell time.' We used it again. It's still working.
Ash said 'okay,' and later brought me a snack without a word. I'd say it's a perfect system.

choices.label: That's smart.
reaction: Smart and gentle. It lets me protect myself without hurting her. Before, I'd just vanish.
Now I ask. And she says okay. That's all I ever wanted. A simple 'okay.'

choices.label: Snacks help.
reaction: Snacks always help. A snack says 'I'm here, I'm not mad.' I've started leaving snacks too.
Ash says 'you're getting good at this.' I'm still not sure I am.

lines: Hot take: Trust isn't a leap. It's a lot of tiny steps in the same direction.

choices.label: That's a good way to see it.
reaction: I think so too. I've never been good at leaps. But steps? I can do steps.
One tea, one note, one 'okay.' It adds up.

choices.label: Some people leap though.
reaction: Some do. I admire that. I just think the people who step slowly can also arrive.
It just takes longer. And it's usually quieter.

lines: Hot take: Being guarded isn't the same as being closed.

choices.label: That's a good distinction.
reaction: It took me years to realize that. A guard is just a gate.
A gate can open. A wall can't. I'm a gate. Ash knows the code. Slowly.

choices.label: Hm, interesting.
reaction: Thanks. I'm still working on it. Some days I feel like a wall.
Some days like a gate. Most days like a gate with a nap.

lines: Hot take: The best love stories have a lot of boring, kind moments in them.

choices.label: Totally.
reaction: The boring ones are the real ones. Tea. A nod. A shared silence.
I'd take a thousand of those over one big dramatic scene.

choices.label: I like some drama too.
reaction: Fair. Drama has its charms. But for me, drama feels like a storm.
Boring feels like shelter. I've had enough storms. I'll take the shelter.

lines: What's something small your partner does that makes you feel safe?
I'm trying to learn what 'safe' looks like for other people.

choices.label: They check in on me.
reaction: Check-ins. Yes. Ash does that. A quick 'how are you?' that doesn't need a long answer.
Just a tiny hello for the heart.

choices.label: They keep their promises.
reaction: Keeping promises. That's my number one. Even the small ones.
'I'll bring tea.' And then she does. That's the whole foundation of trust. Tea.

lines: Do you and your partner ever need space from each other?
I'm curious how other people ask for it.

choices.label: We just say it honestly.
reaction: Honestly. That's it. No big speech.
Just 'I need a little space.' It's simple, but it's hard. I'm practicing.
Ash and I have 'shell time.'

choices.label: It's tricky, we're still figuring it out.
reaction: Same. It's a skill. Like walking on stilts. You wobble, and then you improve.
Please be gentle with yourself. I'm trying to do the same.

lines: What does your partner do that makes you feel seen?
I'm collecting. For a project.

choices.label: They notice small things.
reaction: Small things. I like that. Ash noticed I like my tea at exactly the right temperature.
I never said it. She just knew. It made me feel like a person.

choices.label: They remember what I said.
reaction: Remembering. That's huge. People forget so easily. Ash remembers I said I dislike loud noises.
So she brings a quiet picnic. That's what attention looks like.

dialogues.scene: Dillon uncurls fully, which you've never seen before.
lines: Okay. I want you to see this.
This is my shell, open. All the way. Just for a second. It's a lot. Please don't make it weird.

choices.label: Thank you for showing me.
reaction: ...Okay. That's enough. That felt like jumping off a small cliff.
But it was a soft one. I'm curling back up now. But thank you.
For being kind about it.

choices.label: Smile gently.
reaction: ...That's all I needed. A gentle smile. No comment.
You're very good at not making things weird. I'm going to remember this. Maybe.

dialogues.scene: Ash appears carrying two cups of tea and sets one down quietly next to Dillon.
lines: Hi. You must be the friend. Dillon told me about you.
Thanks for being patient with Dillon. It means a lot. I'm Ash.

choices.label: Dillon's lovely.
reaction: I know. Dillon doesn't say it, but I think so too.
Dillon has a very careful heart. I'm honored to be near it.

choices.label: Nice to meet you, Ash.
reaction: Nice to meet you. Want some tea? Dillon will pretend not to be nervous.
He's very good at it. He's also very bad at it. It's endearing.
